The Active subverse column in the daily Popular Posting Times submission isn't the most active subverse for that hour. If I did it that way, it would almost always be v/news, v/politics, v/whatever etc.

Instead, it is the subverse which is most active in that hour relative to its average posting rate throughout the day. I calculate the average posting rate per hour for each subverse, then look for the subverse which exceeds that average rate by the largest number for that hour.

For example (using data for Popular Posting Times - 2017-04-28) suppose v/Identitarian received 59 posts throughout the day that's 59 / 24 = 2.46 average posts per hour. Good article.

I dislike French politics and French government for various reasons. Their seminal document on democracy "La Declaration des droits de l'homme and du citoyen" from 1789 reads at first blush like a similar document to the US's Declaration of Independence conjoined with the Bill of Rights. But it is actually quite different and that is the wellspring of many fundamental issues.

While I'd be happy to say more on the subject it is best fit for another conversation. The point is simply that even what is considered right wing in France is to me something approaching hard core socialism. There are definitely aspects of Marine Le Pen's programs and rhetoric that I prefer. But in all honesty, the best candidate for France probably was Fallon.

Where I differ with Le Pen and her party is on economics and differences in state control and individual liberty. Their brand of right wing does not resemble the American right wing at all. And I fear Macron will win. That will be a shame, because he is truly horrible. Le Pen would be far, far preferable.

Nothing to do but wait and watch, I guess.
